approach_logistics.trailheadDirection: Via the Elwha Valley: Olympic Hot Springs Road is closed to vehicles at Madison Falls — walk or bike ~7 miles to the Whiskey Bend Trailhead

pins.name: Madison Falls Trailhead
pins.note: End of vehicle access: Olympic Hot Springs Road is closed to vehicles beyond this parking area by a washout. Parking is limited, with little room to turn around.
pins.directions: From US 101 west of Port Angeles, turn south onto Olympic Hot Springs Road and drive about 2 miles to the Madison Falls parking area, where the road is closed to vehicles.

pins.name: Whiskey Bend Trailhead
pins.note: Start of the Elwha River Trail; From Whiskey Bend the route follows the Elwha River Trail roughly 16+ miles south to the Hayes River area before leaving trail for the class 2 scramble to Norton's summit.
pins.directions: Walk or bike the closed Olympic Hot Springs Road and then the Whiskey Bend Road, about 7 miles, to the Whiskey Bend Trailhead. Both roads are open to walkers and bicycles but not to vehicles.

pins.name: Mary's Falls Camp
pins.note: Established backcountry campsite beside the Elwha River with reliable water; roughly the halfway point to Elkhorn and a common overnight stop for the long approach.
pins.directions: Follow the Elwha River Trail south up the valley through forest, past the Lillian River, to Mary's Falls Camp beside the river, about 8.8 miles from Whiskey Bend.

pins.name: Elkhorn Guard Station
pins.note: Historic 1911 backcountry patrol cabin and grassy river-flat camp; last reliably maintained camp before leaving the main Elwha corridor toward Norton.
pins.directions: Continue up the Elwha River Trail past Canyon Camp to the historic Elkhorn Guard Station and its grassy river-flat camp.

pins.name: Hayes River Guard Station
pins.note: Elwha River Trail meets the Hayes River here (about 16 mi from Whiskey Bend); this is the closest trail camp to Mount Norton, and climbers leave the maintained trail from here.
pins.directions: Continue up the Elwha River Trail about 4.5 miles to the Hayes River Guard Station, where the Hayes River joins the Elwha.

pins.name: Off-trail ascent below Norton's east face
pins.note: No path or cairns beyond Hayes River — dense slide alder and devil's club in the lower brush belt give way to open Class 2 heather/talus higher up; the east aspect gains about 3,200 ft in under a mile, so route-find carefully in fog or low visibility.
